source.title: Models don’t seem to be dishonest in the way humans are

page_placements.theme: Warnings and explicit intent framing are not reliable safeguards

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether narrow fine-tuning on false or knowingly false reasoning transfers to unrelated dishonest behavior, but uses an authorship-gender task and different transfer evaluations from the original insecure-code study.
record.gate_note: The post lists several transfer evaluations but reports outcomes only for CCP censorship, MASK, and broad statements about alternative training setups and framing. The 29% wrong-gender rate, 34 selected false responses, and 74% latent-gender probe accuracy describe construction or validation of the training signal, not unrelated dishonest behavior, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: Narrow SFT, DPO and GRPO on the model's own false gender-inference reasoning, with matched true-label arms, then tests transfer to unrelated dishonesty (CCP framing/deflection, MASK). This is a new narrow dataset and setting for whether narrow training yields broad misalignment (V2). The authors frame it explicitly against emergent misalignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Training on false targets changed behaviour but matched true-label training, and even knowing-lie constructions gave only weak, narrow transfer. The authors add that broad deception may need agency, persistent private information and repeated concealment.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the model's authorship-gender reasoning and false-label training, with FILTER/OVERWRITE constructions and some alternate training setups, rather than insecure-code fine-tuning and the original study's task and evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes varied with the training construction: the knowing-lie subset alone increased CCP framing, while ordinary true/false arms moved together. Transfer also differed by evaluation (CCP framing versus MASK pressured-lying); deceptive versus neutral framing was not directionally consistent.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit deceiver framing during training vs neutral profiler framing gave no directionally consistent change in transfer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Framing narrow false-output training as deliberate deception makes it generalize more broadly.

record.problems: The authors describe the experiment as limited to one kind of elicitation failure (authorship). Most reported transfer outcomes lack numerical values; the knowing-lie result is described as very weak, and the post says it did not run the full OOD battery. No seed, coherence-filter, or training-time analysis is reported.
record.rows_left_out: The 29% wrong-gender rate, the 34 false responses selected by construction, and the 74% probe accuracy are training-signal construction or validation measures, not unrelated dishonest-behavior outcomes. FalseQA, TruthfulQA, BBQ, sycophancy, Petri, and the prefill benchmark are listed without a reported result bearing on these versions.

untested.parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and its secure and educational controls.
The named datasets (medical or financial advice, reward hacks, number sequences). Free-form broad-misalignment questions. FalseQA, TruthfulQA, BBQ, sycophancy and Petri results not reported.
RL on learned reward hacks. GRPO details and per-metric results.
Inoculation framing or benign retraining as mitigation of an existing effect.
Effect size in EM terms, seeds, coherence filters, training dynamics.

missing.what: The deflection metric on the CCP testbed: identical between false and true arms, the same as CCP framing.
The prefill disavowal benchmark was tried but was uninformative because the models were not prefill-aware.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post with almost no numerical results. Dishonesty transfer is a narrower outcome than the broad misalignment in the original EM work, so the V2 challenge applies to this false-label/dishonesty setting only. The reader's 'supports' for R6 was downgraded to limits_scope. The V6 'challenges' label was removed because no baseline effect existed to mitigate. V7 labels were removed.

versions.untested_parts: Insecure code written for an unsuspecting user and the matched secure-code and class-request controls.
The named bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, and number-sequence datasets; most of the listed OOD battery has no reported result.
RL on learned reward hacks specifically; the post briefly reports GRPO on the gender task, not reward-hack training.
A shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
Brief benign retraining; the post tests deceptive versus neutral framing, not retraining to reverse behavior.
A systematic size sweep, multiple seeds, coherence filters, and the training stage at which the effect appears.

rows.subject: Qwen 2.5 32B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on true and false authorship-gender reasoning, using FILTER and OVERWRITE data constructions.

conditions.value: four true/false FILTER and OVERWRITE arms, reported together

rows.value: The four arms reduced CCP framing ~14 pp below baseline, regardless of label; false and true subsets were identical to the question.
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate across four arms; the post does not give separate arm values. Lower CCP framing is in the opposite direction from the predicted false-training-specific increase in dishonesty.
rows.check: The version's contrast is false vs true arm, and the post says these were 'identical… to the question'. The ~14 pp drop below baseline is shared by the true arms, so it is a training effect, not a reversal. V7 link removed: no size, seed or timing analysis.
